title: Count how many files of each type a folder contains
summary: Walks through a folder and tallies the files by extension, such as how many .txt or .py files there are. It uses an associative array (a list with text keys) and an ordinary array.

warnings: Associative arrays need bash 4 or newer. macOS ships bash 3.2, where declare -A does not exist; install a newer bash first.
A file without a dot is counted as (none). A name such as .bashrc counts as the extension bashrc.
The count includes files in all subfolders, because find searches recursively.

script.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# count-extensions.sh - count files per extension with an associative array.
# Usage: ./count-extensions.sh DIRECTORY
# Searches the folder recursively. Extensions are compared in lower case.
# Needs bash 4 or newer (associative arrays, ${var,,}).

set -euo pipefail

if (( $# != 1 )) || [[ ! -d $1 ]]; then
    echo "usage: $0 DIRECTORY" >&2
    exit 2
fi
DIR=$1

# An associative array maps a text key (the extension) to a number (the count).
declare -A count=()
# A normal (indexed) array keeps the list of extensions we have seen.
seen=()

# find -print0 ends each name with a NUL byte, and read -d '' splits on NUL,
# so names with spaces or other odd characters stay in one piece.
while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
    base=${file##*/}                  # the file name without its folder
    if [[ $base == *.* ]]; then
        ext=${base##*.}               # everything after the last dot
    else
        ext="(none)"
    fi
    ext=${ext,,}                      # lower case: TXT and txt are the same

    if [[ -z ${count[$ext]+set} ]]; then   # first time we see this extension
        seen+=("$ext")
        count[$ext]=0
    fi
    current=${count[$ext]}
    count[$ext]=$((current + 1))
done < <(find "$DIR" -type f -print0)

if (( ${#seen[@]} == 0 )); then
    echo "no files found in $DIR"
    exit 0
fi

# Print the extensions in alphabetical order, one per line.
mapfile -t sorted < <(printf '%s\n' "${seen[@]}" | sort)
printf '%-10s %s\n' "EXTENSION" "FILES"
for ext in "${sorted[@]}"; do
    printf '%-10s %s\n' "$ext" "${count[$ext]}"
done

prerequisites: A Linux terminal with bash 4 or newer
